 Dana Cline Discusses Medicare Enrollment and Plan Benefits 
 Medicare enrollment deadline December 7th. 
 Studio 3 - Cline Insurance By Angela Evans Published : Nov. 17, 2026 at 5:22 PM CST | Updated : moments ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Medicare’s annual enrollment period ends Dec. 7, and Dana Cline visited Studio 3 to discuss options for people reviewing their coverage and planning for the year ahead.
 Medicare’s annual open enrollment runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7. During that time, eligible beneficiaries can make changes to Medicare Advantage and prescription drug coverage. Changes generally take effect Jan. 1.
 Options after annual enrollment
 People who are already enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan have another opportunity to make a change during the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period, from Jan. 1 through March 31. They can switch to another Medicare Advantage plan or return to Original Medicare and join a separate drug plan. Generally, only one change is allowed during this period.
 Cline suggested contacting an agent for help reviewing changes. To contact Cline Insurance, visit www.clineinsurancecompany.com/ .
 Compare more than extra benefits
 Cline discussed supplemental benefits that may be offered by Medicare Advantage plans, such as dental, vision, hearing, fitness, over-the-counter items and, for some eligible members, healthy food benefits. These benefits vary by plan and may have eligibility restrictions.
 A healthy food benefit is not guaranteed for every enrollee; some benefits require qualifying chronic conditions and confirmation of eligibility. Cline encouraged viewers not to choose a plan based on a food benefit alone, but to check whether their doctors are in the plan’s network and their medications are covered.
 Other enrollment opportunities
 Some people may qualify for a special enrollment period outside the usual annual window. For example, someone with a qualifying chronic condition may be able to join an available Chronic Condition Special Needs Plan that serves that condition. Eligibility and timing depend on individual circumstances.
 Cline also discussed Medicare Supplement Insurance, or Medigap. People can apply at other times of the year, but acceptance and pricing may depend on medical underwriting unless they have a guaranteed-issue right or other applicable protection. Medicare’s six-month Medigap open enrollment period, which begins when a person is 65 or older and enrolled in Part B, provides important protections.
